note: Separate overlay contract for the Nephilim tyrant's club slam warning. It is independent of the 64 px boss cell. The hit area belongs to Core; this file only says how the warning looks and where it must be placed.

core.owner: Core (single writer). Values quoted from docs/harness/r03-implementation-01.md as technical tuning, not balance-final
core.shape: circle, fixed target locked at warning start, one hit at impact
core.note: if Core changes the radius, the runtime ring follows it; nothing here is re-tuned by hand

placement.rule: at runtime the boundary is drawn procedurally from the Core target and radius through the shared world projection (the same one actors use). The art never decides where the edge is.
placement.boundary: the OUTER edge of the black line is the hit boundary. Nothing is drawn outside it, so the picture never makes the area look larger than the hit; the white line sits just inside the black one

nominalRadiusPx.meaning: 1.2 world units x PPU 32 at SOURCE asset density only. It is not a Unity screen-pixel radius; the screen radius is whatever the shared projection gives for 1.2 world units

mustNot: scale or pad the ring so the visible edge differs from the projected radius
fit the ring into the 64 px boss cell
add a fill or glow outside the boundary

lines.name: inner
lines.from: 2 source px inside the boundary, inward

style.widthRule: widths scale with the actor pixel scale (source px x scale) and never drop below 1 screen px each
style.fill: none. The ground stays visible inside the circle
style.motion: static for the whole 1.2 s: no blinking, no pulsing, no full-screen flash. Progress is shown by the boss pose (windup frames), not by the ring
style.lowFx: always shown: the ring is gameplay information, not an optional effect; same in low-effects, muted and small-window modes
style.readability: black outer + white inner reads on dark grass, light path and in greyscale

assets.use: reference rendering of the style at nominal source density (radius 38.4 source px about the cell centre) for review boards and as a sanity picture for the runtime ring. A texture fallback is allowed only if it is placed and scaled so its black outer edge equals the projected radius

cracks and dust at the locked target on the impact tick (the boss may be far from the target). Drawn centred on the target at actor pixel scale; all content stays inside 34 of 38.4 nominal px, so it never reaches past the boundary. Silent-safe: it is the visual 'it hit here' after the ring disappears
